## Objective
- Build a complete, playable hyperrealistic open-world browser game where typed prompts alter and generate the world.

## Requirements
- Anything typed should produce a corresponding in-world effect.
- Support desktop and mobile play, open-world movement, command interface, weather/time effects, and generated objects.
- Capture and inspect screenshots at widths no greater than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Use vanilla HTML/CSS and Three.js.
- Interpret prompts locally without an external AI model.
- Build a cinematic landscape with terrain, lake, village, forest, weather, particles, minimap, and mobile controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` implementing the game shell, responsive interface, world generation, movement, prompt interpretation, weather/time changes, and related controls.
- Fixed JavaScript syntax errors in `game.js`; `node --check game.js` now passes.
- Started a local server on port 4173; `http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html` returns HTTP 200.

### Active
- Verifying browser rendering and diagnosing why the captured page appears to retain the loading overlay.

### Blocked
- No Playwright package is installed. A Chromium screenshot was captured, but its view showed mostly a blue scene with the loading overlay still present; browser runtime initialization remains unconfirmed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` startup code around `buildWorld()` and the loading overlay; check for browser module/runtime errors.
2. Re-capture and inspect a screenshot at 1280px or narrower after resolving initialization.
3. Check mobile rendering and interaction if browser verification succeeds.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main page structure and UI.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, prompt system, controls, and startup logic.
- `/tmp/elsewhere-desktop.png`: Initial desktop screenshot, currently showing an apparent loading/rendering issue.
- `/tmp/chromium.log`: Chromium output from the initial screenshot capture.

## Important Context
- Current syntax fix in `game.js` wraps the prompt-category checks in nested braces; syntax validation passes.
- `game.js` calls `buildWorld()` at line 232, `animate()` at line 274, and hides the loading overlay after 700 ms at line 275.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable hyperrealistic open-world browser game where typed prompts alter and generate the world.

## Requirements
- Anything typed should produce a corresponding in-world effect.
- Support desktop and mobile play, open-world movement, command interface, weather/time effects, and generated objects.
- Capture and inspect screenshots at widths no greater than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Use vanilla HTML/CSS and Three.js.
- Interpret prompts locally without an external AI model.
- Build a cinematic landscape with terrain, lake, village, forest, weather, particles, minimap, and mobile controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game shell, responsive interface, generated world, movement, prompt interpretation, weather/time effects, and controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed startup crash `Cannot access 'particles' before initialization` by moving animation startup until after `particles` initialization and replacing the earlier frame loop with the enhanced loop.
- `node --check game.js` passes.

- (none)

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game where typed prompts change an open world.
- Address the user’s feedback that important interactions are missing: “I can't blow stuff up or make the sky rainbow”.

## Requirements
- Anything typed should produce a corresponding in-world effect.
- Support desktop and mobile play, open-world movement, weather/time effects, and generated objects.
- Capture and inspect screenshots at widths no greater than 1280px.
- Make explosions/destruction and rainbow skies work through typed prompts.

## Decisions
- Use vanilla HTML/CSS and Three.js; interpret prompts locally without an external AI model.
- Existing world includes terrain, lake, village, forest, weather, particles, minimap, and mobile controls.
- Improve prompt interpretation to support broader user phrasing and visible effects.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, responsive UI, world generation, movement, prompt interpretation, weather/time effects, and controls in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed startup crash `Cannot access 'particles' before initialization`; `node --check game.js` passes.
- Verified rendering at 1280×800 and 390×844; tested suggested/custom prompts and keyboard movement without JavaScript runtime errors.

### Active
- Implement explosion/destruction prompts and rainbow sky prompts; existing interpretation only removes the last generated prop for remove/delete/destroy/erase, while sky coloring handles only single colors and does not support rainbow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and update `game.js` prompt parsing so phrases such as “blow stuff up” trigger visible explosions and destruction, not just removal of one generated prop.
2. Add a visible rainbow sky effect that updates background/fog and remains coherent with time/weather controls.
3. Test representative prompts in-browser, check rendered results, and confirm no runtime errors.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/elsewhere-desktop.png`: latest desktop capture at 1280×800.
- `/tmp/elsewhere-mobile.png`: latest mobile capture at 390×844.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: world simulation, particles, prompt parsing, and generated effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game UI and prompt form.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: responsive layout and visual styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server is running at `http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html`.
- Earlier browser interaction test showed generic prompts create objects, but did not validate explosion or rainbow behavior.
- Chromium logs include environment-related DBus warnings and WebGL `GPU stall due to ReadPixels`; no JavaScript runtime errors in the latest capture logs.
